image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a male mallard duck (drake) floating on water. The duck is facing left but has its head turned back to rest on its own back, a common preening or resting posture. The iridescent green head, white neck ring, yellow bill, and grey/brown patterned body plumage are clearly visible. The tail features the characteristic curled black central feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellow-green in color, matching the description perfectly.
The visible eye is dark and distinct against the green head plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body appears compact and floats naturally on the water surface. The plumage texture looks dense and consistent with waterproof feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and grey/brown mottled body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely submerged or occluded by the body and water; they are not visible in this frame.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing broad structure and pointed tip geometry consistent with a duck wing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear right, featuring the distinctive upward-curling black central feathers typical of male mallards.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard Drake) and verify fine-grained plumage details against ImageNet classes.
To check for edge bleeding between the complex feather textures and the water background, ensuring no 'melting' artifacts.
To assess overall texture consistency, lighting realism, and detect any subtle generative noise or blur.
To verify the physical interaction between the duck's body and the water surface (displacement/reflection) is geometrically sound.

focus_areas: Feather texture consistency and edge sharpness against water
Anatomical correctness of the twisted neck/head posture
Water displacement and reflection realism around the body
Integrity of the white neck ring boundary
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the junction where the head meets the body. In AI images, this area often shows fusion artifacts when the head is turned back. Verify if the white neck ring remains continuous and logically placed despite the twist. Check if the water ripples radiate naturally from the body's contact points.
